description: Make provides visual no-code automation for connecting applications and building cross-system workflows.
description_cn: 提供可视化无代码自动化平台，用于连接不同应用并构建跨系统工作流。

tools.description: Lists the Make zone, organizations, and teams reachable through this connection, including private spaces. Most Make resources belong to a team; other tools require the organizationId and teamId returned here. Call this first when you need ids. A private space id is valid wherever a teamId is accepted.
tools.name: environment_get

tools.description: List scenarios (scenarios): List all scenarios for a team. Results can be narrowed to one folder (optionally including its subfolders) and/or to scenarios carrying at least one of the given scenario labels. Returned scenarios include their assigned labels.
tools.name: scenarios_list

tools.description: Get scenario (scenarios): Get a scenario and its blueprint by ID.
tools.name: scenarios_get

tools.description: Create scenario (scenarios): Create a new scenario from a blueprint. Verify every module name in the blueprint via app-modules_list before creating — never invent module identifiers. The created scenario starts INACTIVE: call scenarios_activate before scenarios_run can execute it.
tools.name: scenarios_create

tools.description: Update scenario (scenarios): Update a scenario. The `blueprint` parameter wholesale-REPLACES the existing blueprint (no merging): always fetch the current blueprint with scenarios_get first, edit that JSON, and send the complete result. Tool scenarios (created via tools_create) cannot be blueprint-edited with this tool — use tools_update.
tools.name: scenarios_update

tools.description: Delete scenario (scenarios): Delete a scenario.
tools.name: scenarios_delete

tools.description: Activate scenario (scenarios): Activate a scenario. Required before scenarios_run can execute it. If this fails with 'Scenario is already running', the scenario is already active — treat that as success and do not retry.
tools.name: scenarios_activate

tools.description: Deactivate scenario (scenarios): Deactivate a scenario. If this fails with 'Scenario is not running', the scenario is already inactive — treat that as success and do not retry.
tools.name: scenarios_deactivate

tools.description: Run scenario (scenarios): Execute a scenario with optional input data. The scenario must be ACTIVE — a run of an inactive scenario fails with 'Scenario is not activated', so call scenarios_activate first (newly created scenarios start inactive). Returns an executionId: after a failed or suspicious run, inspect it with executions_get-detail BEFORE retrying or editing the scenario. A scenario cannot run twice concurrently — on 'Scenario is already being executed', wait for the running execution instead of retrying.
tools.name: scenarios_run

tools.description: Replay scenario execution (scenarios): Replay a past execution of a scenario, re-running it with the trigger data the original execution received. Get candidate execution IDs from executions_list. Only executions whose input data is still stored can be replayed — 'Execution is not replayable' means that execution's data has expired or was never stored, so try a MORE RECENT execution instead of retrying the same one. Only the first ID in executionIds is replayed. The scenario must be ACTIVE. A replay starts a real execution and consumes operations exactly like scenarios_run; it returns the executionId of the NEW execution, which you can inspect with executions_get-detail.
tools.name: scenarios_replay

tools.description: Get scenario interface (scenarios): Get the interface for a scenario.
tools.name: scenarios_interface

tools.description: Set scenario interface (scenarios): Update the interface for a scenario.
tools.name: scenarios_set-interface

tools.description: List executions (executions): List executions for a scenario.
tools.name: executions_list

tools.description: Get execution detail (executions): Get the full per-module detail of an execution: the inputs and outputs of each module, the failing module and its error. ALWAYS call this after a failed or suspicious run BEFORE retrying or editing the scenario. For lightweight status/duration metadata only, use executions_get instead.
tools.name: executions_get-detail

tools.description: Get execution (executions): Get execution metadata only: status, duration, operations consumed and error class — NOT per-module inputs/outputs. To see what each module did or why a run failed, use executions_get-detail instead.
tools.name: executions_get

tools.description: Search execution data (executions): Full-text search the input/output data of scenario executions across an organization (all teams you can access, or one team via teamId). Returns matching executions, each with up to 5 matching module IO records and highlighted snippets. Use it to find which runs handled a given value (an order ID, an email, an error text). Wrap the query in double quotes for an exact phrase. from/to apply at UTC-day granularity, so narrow them to keep the search fast. Requires the Pro plan or above.
tools.name: executions_search-io-data

tools.description: Count execution data matches (executions): Count how many scenarios and executions across an organization (all teams you can access, or one team via teamId) have input/output data matching a full-text query, with a per-scenario breakdown. Use it to size a search before calling executions_search-io-data, or to see which scenarios handled a given value. Wrap the query in double quotes for an exact phrase. from/to apply at UTC-day granularity; the last 7 days are searched when both are omitted.
tools.name: executions_count-io-data-matches

tools.description: Search data of one execution (executions): Full-text search the input/output data of a single execution and return every matching module IO record with highlighted snippets, plus the execution metadata. Use it after executions_search-io-data to see all matches in one run (that tool returns at most 5 per execution). Wrap the query in double quotes for an exact phrase. from/to apply at UTC-day granularity and default to the last 7 days, so pass a window that covers the execution for older runs. Requires the Pro plan or above.
tools.name: executions_search-io-data-in-execution

tools.description: Search executions (executions): Search executions across an organization (all teams you can access, or one team via teamId), newest first, by time window, status, scenario, or a substring of the error message (matches are highlighted). Use it to find failed or warning runs across many scenarios at once; for a single scenario, executions_list is enough. from/to apply at UTC-day granularity; the last 7 days are searched by default.
tools.name: executions_search

tools.description: List folders (folders): List scenario folders for a team. If you do not know the teamId, find it via organizations_list (each organization lists its teams) or teams_list, or ask the user — never guess IDs.
tools.name: folders_list

tools.description: Create folder (folders): Create a new folder.
tools.name: folders_create

tools.description: Update folder (folders): Update an existing folder.
tools.name: folders_update

tools.description: Delete folder (folders): Delete a folder.
tools.name: folders_delete

tools.description: List scenario labels (scenario-labels): List a team's scenario label catalog, including how many scenarios carry each label. Scenario labels are [REDACTED] tags that can be assigned to scenarios, independent of folders. If you do not know the teamId, find it via organizations_list (each organization lists its teams) or teams_list, or ask the user — never guess IDs.
tools.name: scenario-labels_list

tools.description: Create scenario label (scenario-labels): Create a new scenario label in a team. Labels are [REDACTED] tags that can be assigned to scenarios. If you do not know the teamId, call users_me to learn it.
tools.name: scenario-labels_create

tools.description: Update scenario label (scenario-labels): Update the name, colour, or description of an existing scenario label. Provide at least one property to change; omitted properties are left unchanged. Changes are reflected on every scenario carrying the label.
tools.name: scenario-labels_update

tools.description: Delete scenario label (scenario-labels): Delete a scenario label. The label is removed from the team catalog and unassigned from every scenario carrying it. This cannot be undone.
tools.name: scenario-labels_delete

tools.description: Assign scenario label (scenario-labels): Assign a scenario label to a scenario. The label and the scenario must belong to the same team. Assigning an already-assigned label succeeds without changes. To label many scenarios, call this tool once per scenario.
tools.name: scenario-labels_assign

tools.description: Unassign scenario label (scenario-labels): Remove a scenario label from a scenario. Removing an already-absent assignment succeeds without changes. The label itself stays in the team catalog.
tools.name: scenario-labels_unassign

tools.description: List webhooks/mailhooks (hooks): List webhooks/mailhooks for a specific team.
tools.name: hooks_list

tools.description: List organization webhooks/mailhooks (hooks): List webhooks/mailhooks across all teams of an organization that you can view, including private spaces, with their team ID and URL. Filter by team, a name substring, type, whether they are assigned to a scenario, or whether they are enabled. Returns 50 hooks by default; use limit and offset to page. Use it to find a hook when you do not know its team; for a single team, hooks_list is enough.
tools.name: hooks_list-for-organization

tools.description: Get webhook/mailhook (hooks): Get details of a specific webhook/mailhook.
tools.name: hooks_get

tools.description: Create webhook/mailhook (hooks): Create a new webhook/mailhook.
tools.name: hooks_create

tools.description: Update webhook/mailhook (hooks): Update an existing webhook/mailhook.
tools.name: hooks_update

tools.description: Delete webhook/mailhook (hooks): Delete a webhook/mailhook.
tools.name: hooks_delete

tools.description: List webhook queue items (hook-incomings): List items currently waiting in a webhook's processing queue — payloads the webhook received but hasn't handed off to a scenario yet (e.g. because the scenario isn't active).
tools.name: hook-incomings_list

tools.description: Get webhook queue stats (hook-incomings): Get the current size and limit of a webhook's processing queue.
tools.name: hook-incomings_stats

tools.description: Get webhook queue item detail (hook-incomings): Get the full detail of a single queued item, including its payload when available. Confidential hooks omit payload data.
tools.name: hook-incomings_get

tools.description: Delete webhook queue items (hook-incomings): Delete items from a webhook's processing queue. Specify `ids` to delete specific items, or `all: true` (with `confirmed: true`) to clear the entire queue. An item currently being processed cannot be deleted.
tools.name: hook-incomings_delete

tools.description: List data structures (data-structures): List data structures for a team.
tools.name: data-structures_list

tools.description: Get data structure (data-structures): Get details of a specific data structure.
tools.name: data-structures_get

tools.description: Create data structure (data-structures): Create a new data structure.
tools.name: data-structures_create

tools.description: Update data structure (data-structures): Update an existing data structure.
tools.name: data-structures_update

tools.description: Delete data structure (data-structures): Delete a data structure.
tools.name: data-structures_delete

tools.description: List connections (connections): List connections for a team.
tools.name: connections_list

tools.description: Get connection (connections): Get details of a specific connection.
tools.name: connections_get

tools.description: List keys (keys): List all keys for a team.
tools.name: keys_list

tools.description: Get key (keys): Get details of a specific key.
tools.name: keys_get

tools.description: Delete key (keys): Delete a key.
tools.name: keys_delete

tools.description: List credential requests (credential-requests): Retrieve a list of credential requests. Each request can contain multiple credentials (connections and API keys). Filter by team, user, provider, status, or name to find specific requests.
tools.name: credential-requests_list

tools.description: Get credential request details (credential-requests): Retrieve detailed information about a specific credential request by its ID. Returns all associated credentials with their authorization status, provider configuration, user details, and authorization URLs for pending credentials. Use this to check the state of credentials within a request.
tools.name: credential-requests_get

tools.description: Delete credential request (credential-requests): Permanently delete a credential request and all associated credentials (connections and API keys) by ID. Any scenarios using connections from this request will lose access to the corresponding services. This action cannot be undone.
tools.name: credential-requests_delete

tools.description: Decline credential (credential-requests): Decline a credential authorization request by ID, setting its status to "declined" and preventing it from being authorized. An optional reason can be provided to explain the decision. This operation is idempotent - declining an already-declined credential has no additional effect.
tools.name: credential-requests_credential-decline

tools.description: Delete credential (credential-requests): Delete a credential (e.g., revoke OAuth tokens or remove stored API keys) and reset its state to pending. Use this when a credential needs re-authorization with updated permissions, tokens have become stale, or you want to force re-authentication. After deletion, the credential can be authorized again through the normal flow.
tools.name: credential-requests_credential-delete

tools.description: Create credential request (credential-requests): Create a credential request for the currently authenticated user to set up connections and keys. This will return a URL where the user can authorize the credentials, so that they can be used in scenarios.
tools.name: credential-requests_create

tools.description: Create credential request by connection/key types (credential-requests): Create a credential request for one or more connections (OAuth) and/or keys (API keys) by their type identifiers (e.g. "google", "slack", "apikeyauth"). Use this when you know the exact connection or key types needed. The response includes the created request, an array of credentials associated with the request, and a publicUri where the end-user must go to authorize the requested credentials. At least one connection or one key must be provided.
tools.name: credential-requests_create-by-credentials

tools.description: Extend connection OAuth scopes (credential-requests): Add new OAuth scopes to an existing connection. Use this when a connection exists but lacks the permissions (scopes) needed for a specific operation. Creates a credential request that the end-user must authorize via the returned publicUri to grant the additional scopes. Fails if all requested scopes are already present on the connection — that error means the connection already satisfies the requirement: treat it as success and use the connection as-is; do not retry.
tools.name: credential-requests_extend-connection

tools.description: List app modules with credentials (credential-requests): List all modules of a given Make app (and version) that require credentials, along with the required credential type and OAuth scopes. Use this to discover which modules exist for an app before constructing a credential request — the returned `id` values are what you pass in `credentials[].appModules` for `credential-requests_create`. For custom/SDK apps, prefix the app name with `app#` (e.g. `app#my-custom-app`).
tools.name: credential-requests_list-app-modules-with-creds

tools.description: List private spaces (private-spaces): List the private spaces of an organization. Requires the organization's private-spaces feature to be enabled (error IM903 otherwise) and the 'personal team manage' permission. Private spaces cannot be created or deleted through the API — they are provisioned automatically by organization settings.
tools.name: private-spaces_list

tools.description: Get private space (private-spaces): Get details of a specific private space, including usage totals (operations, transfer, centicredits). Callers who are not members of the space receive a 404 even when the space exists.

tools.description: Update private space (private-spaces): Update a private space's operations limit. Set operationsLimit to null to remove the limit (unlimited); the transfer limit is derived automatically. When the new limit is below the space's current consumption the call fails with IM004 unless 'confirmed' is true — confirming pauses the space.

tools.description: List custom property structures (custom-property-structures): List the custom property structures defined for an organization. Requires the organization's custom-properties feature to be enabled (error IM027 otherwise). At most one structure can exist per combination of associated type, belonger type, and belonger ID — currently 'scenario'/'organization' is the only supported combination — and structures cannot be deleted through the API.

tools.description: Create custom property structure (custom-property-structures): Create a custom property structure for an organization. Only one structure can exist per (associatedType, belongerType, belongerId) combination — creating a second one for the same organization fails with IM005. Once created, a structure cannot be deleted through the API. Use 'scenario' as associatedType and 'organization' as belongerType — these are the only values the API currently accepts.

tools.description: List custom property structure items (custom-property-structure-items): List the items (field definitions) of a custom property structure. Use custom-property-structures_list to find the structure ID.

tools.description: Create custom property structure item (custom-property-structure-items): Create an item (field definition) in a custom property structure. The item's name and type cannot be changed after creation. `options` is required for the 'dropdown' and 'multiselect' types and not allowed for any other type.
tools.name: custom-property-structure-items_create

tools.description: Update custom property structure item (custom-property-structure-items): Update a custom property structure item. The item's name and type cannot be changed. When updating `options` of a 'dropdown'/'multiselect' item, the new set fully replaces the current one — existing scenario data referencing removed options is not remapped.
tools.name: custom-property-structure-items_update

tools.description: Delete custom property structure item (custom-property-structure-items): Delete a custom property structure item. Deleting an item also deletes any scenario data filled in for it — this is irreversible. If scenarios already have data for the item, the call fails with IM004 unless 'confirmed' is true.

tools.description: Get scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Get the custom properties data filled in for a scenario.

tools.description: Fill in scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Fill in custom properties data for a scenario for the first time. Fails with IM005 if the scenario already has data — use scenario-custom-properties_update or scenario-custom-properties_replace instead. Every item marked required in the custom property structure must be given a value. Use custom-property-structure-items_list to see the available items.

tools.description: Replace scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Replace all custom properties data for a scenario. Fails with IM013 if the scenario has no data yet — use scenario-custom-properties_create first. Every item marked required in the structure must be given a value.
tools.name: scenario-custom-properties_replace

tools.description: Update scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Merge-update custom properties data for a scenario; only the specified items are changed. Fails with IM013 if the scenario has no data yet — use scenario-custom-properties_create first.
tools.name: scenario-custom-properties_update

tools.description: Delete scenario custom properties data (scenario-custom-properties): Delete all custom properties data for a scenario. This is irreversible.
tools.name: scenario-custom-properties_delete

tools.description:
Executes a Make Remote Procedure Call (RPC) with the provided input.
	Before executing an RPC, be sure you know its exact name and the input parameters that should be passed to the 'data' field.
	There is no RPC-listing tool — never guess RPC names. Discover them via 'app-module_get' (requires the
	'apps:read' scope): the module's parameter instructions reference the RPCs it uses (e.g. as '[REDACTED]'
	option sources). If 'app-module_get' is not available in this conversation, ask the user for the exact RPC name.
	You can also use RPCs to provide answers for simple "read" or "list" queries, if the corresponding RPC is available,
	so it's not needed to create a full Tool to achieve such a thing.
tools.name: rpc_execute

tools.description: Based on the user's intention, recommend applications that can assist in achieving their goals. This tool should provide a list of applications that are relevant to the user's needs, including their names and versions.
tools.name: apps_recommend

tools.description:
This tool creates a new Tool in the system based on provided parameters.
It allows users to define custom tools that can be used in various scenarios.
Use it to add new functionalities to the platform by specifying tool details.

Use this tool also when you're tasked to perform a simple action.
It's easier to configure a tool rather than a whole Scenario.

Important! Before creating a tool, call 'app-module_get' to check how the module should actually be mapped,
then create the mapping, and only then create the tool with this mapping.
Even more important is to call 'app-module_get' with the 'instructions' format requested.
That way, you'll get perfect instructions for how to fill in the module's configuration.

Don't create unnecessary inputs. Create them only for values that should be dynamic,
hardcode everything else in the module parameters.

When the Module requires a Credential (Connection or Key) to be set,
list the existing connections or keys of the corresponding type to see if there are any available.
If there are available connections or keys for the Module, ask the user whether they want to use one of the available connections or keys.
When asking this question, also provide the user with an option to not use available connections, and to create a new connection or key instead.
In case user chooses an option to create a new connection or key, you should request the User to provide you with a new Connection or Key, for that, use the Credential Request Create Tool.
In case there are no available connections or keys of the corresponding type for the Module you are creating,
you should also request the User to provide you with a new Connection or Key, for that, use the Credential Request Create Tool.

If you need to run the Tool, use 'scenarios_run', passing the Tool ID as the scenarioId.
Note: a Tool's blueprint cannot be edited via 'scenarios_update' — use 'tools_update' instead.
tools.name: tools_create

tools.description: Retrieves details of a specific Tool by its ID.
tools.name: tools_get

tools.description:
This tool updates an existing Tool's details based on provided parameters.
It allows users to modify the properties of a Tool to keep it up-to-date with changing requirements.
Use it to refine or correct Tool information as needed.
tools.name: tools_update

tools.description:
This tool validates that parameters and mapper collection are correctly configured for a given module in a given app.
Use this tool before creating a new Make Tool or Make Scenario to verify that the configuration of modules is correct.
Use this tool to iterate towards a successful validation result.
Before generating parameters and mapper objects for the module,
learn instructions for filling them in by getting the module detail in the "instructions" format.
Required fields with declared defaults that you omitted are filled automatically, including fields
that only exist after remote resolution; when the result contains "appliedDefaults", the
"normalizedValues" object carries the filled configuration. When "valid" is true, send
"normalizedValues.default" as "parameters" and "normalizedValues.expect" as "mapper" instead of
inventing values for fields you did not see in the schema; when "valid" is false, fix the reported
errors on top of those objects first.
tools.name: validate_module_configuration

tools.description: Validates the Epoch Configuration of particular Trigger Module.
tools.name: validate_epoch_configuration

tools.description: Validates the overall structure of the Scenario Blueprint against the Schema. STRUCTURAL check only — it does NOT verify that module names exist or that module parameters are correct, so a valid blueprint can still fail at scenarios_create with "Module not found". Verify module names via app-modules_list and module configurations via validate_module_configuration.
tools.name: validate_blueprint_schema

tools.description: Validates the Scheduling of the Scenario against the Schema.
tools.name: validate_scheduling_schema

tools.description:
Retrieves markdown documentation for the specific Make App.
Use when configuring Make Apps and Modules and when you need to learn more about the available capabilities.
tools.name: app_documentation_get

tools.description:
This tool validates that hook configuration values are correctly set for a given hook type.
Use this tool before creating a hook to verify that the configuration is correct.
Use this tool to iterate towards a successful validation result.
Before generating values, learn instructions by getting the hook config in the "instructions" format.
tools.name: validate_hook_configuration

tools.description: Use this tool to validate a typed Scenario Interface before applying changes. Either side (`input`, `output`) may be omitted; only the side(s) supplied are validated.

tools.description:
This tool analyzes a given Blueprint and extracts a list of various Connections, Keys, Hooks and other components that are required to be provided in order to map the Blueprint properly.
Use this tool to identify all necessary components to collect before creating a new Make Scenario based on the Blueprint.
The output will help in preparing the Scenario by ensuring all required resources are available.
tools.name: extract_blueprint_components

tools.description: Extracts the list of Components required by the particular Module. Use to identify what Connections, Keys, Hooks and other resources are needed to work with the Module.
tools.name: extract_module_components

tools.description: Reports which connections and API keys a set of planned modules require, and which of the team's existing credentials already satisfy each requirement (with their ids). Each module returns one SLOT per required credential parameter; a slot's `options` are ALTERNATIVE provider types — any one of them satisfies the slot. Use it to verify a build plan before presenting it: pass every module the scenario will contain. Connections of a matching type whose granted scopes do NOT cover the slot's required scopes are listed separately in `existingInsufficientScopes` (re-auth candidates, never counted as satisfying). Modules that do not exist in the catalog for this organization are returned in `notFound`; credential types whose lookups transiently failed are listed in `failedLookups` (with human-readable diagnostics in `errors`) and must be treated as unknown rather than missing.
tools.name: connection-requirements_get

tools.description:
List pending (uncommitted) changes for a custom app version.

Returns the stack of changes that have been made since the last commit. Each entry includes at least an `id` that can be passed to `custom-apps_changes-fetch` to retrieve the full diff (oldValue/newValue). An empty array means there are no uncommitted changes.

Each entry is decorated with a `label` field that holds the UI-friendly section name as shown in the Make web app — e.g. `code: "api"` is exposed to users as "Communication". Use `label` when describing changes to a human; use `code` when calling other tools.

Only meaningful for approved apps — unapproved apps don't track changes the same way.
tools.name: custom-apps_changes-list

tools.description:
Fetch a single pending change by id, including the previous and proposed values.

Use `custom-apps_changes-list` first to discover change ids, then call this tool with one of those ids to inspect what was changed.

The default `format: "diff"` returns `{ id, group, code, label, diff }` where `diff` is a unified diff string suitable for displaying directly to the user. Pass `format: "raw"` to get the API payload (`{ id, group, code, oldValue, newValue }`) augmented with the same UI-friendly `label` field.
tools.name: custom-apps_changes-fetch

tools.description:
Create new connection or update existing connection. Use mode parameter to specify whether to create or update the connection.

IMPORTANT: Use the custom-apps_get-example tool before creating or updating connection communication (api section) to get an example of different connection communication (api) variants

There are two connection types:
- 'oauth': For all variants of OAuth 1 or 2 flows. In this case, Make handles the OAuth flow
- 'basic': Everyting else, for example:
   - simple API key passing
   - HTTP basic auth
   - passing a token in Bearer header (where no Oauth flow is required, or is done externally to Make)

For CREATE mode: appName, type, and label are required. connectionName is not used (connection ID is auto-generated).
For UPDATE mode: connectionName is required (this is the connection ID, typically the appName or appName with suffix).
tools.name: custom-apps_connections-configure

tools.description:
Create new modules or update existing modules and their sections in a single operation. Use explicit mode parameter to specify whether to create or update the module.

Module typeId values:
- Trigger (polling) [TypeId: 1] - Watch for changes via polling
- Action [TypeId: 4] - Single response endpoint
- Search [TypeId: 9] - Multiple item result
- Universal [TypeId: 12] - Arbitrary API calls
- Instant Trigger (webhook) [TypeId: 10] - Watch for changes via webhook
- Responder [TypeId: 11] - Send processed data back to webhook

For CREATE mode: typeId and label are required. For UPDATE mode: all metadata fields are optional - only provided fields will be updated.
tools.name: custom-apps_modules-configure
